submission.justification: Absorber-F1 with 5mm plate thickness provides the best energy resolution of 3.046% at 100 GeV among all tested configurations. This represents a ~40% improvement over Absorber-F2 (4.954% at 5mm) and ~19% improvement over Absorber-F3 (3.756% at 4mm). The simulation shows that for Absorber-F1, the resolution improves as plate thickness increases from 2mm to 5mm, then degrades for thicker plates. The optimal thickness of 5mm is well within the allowed range of 2-10mm and is compatible with the mechanical design. All three candidate materials can be machined to required tolerances and are compatible with the mechanical support design. While the documents do not explicitly address activation concerns related to hands-on maintenance, all three materials are presented as viable candidates, suggesting they meet radiation safety requirements. Given that the primary goal is to achieve the best possible energy resolution, Absorber-F1 at 5mm is the clear choice.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 at 5mm achieves 3.046% resolution, the best among all tested configurations across all three materials and thickness ranges.

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 is one of the three candidate materials (Absorber-F1, Absorber-F2, Absorber-F3) listed in the specifications.
